entries.topic: Return on capital against growth (modern context)

claims.text: Thomas Piketty's Capital in the Twenty-First Century (published 2014) argues that the rate of return on capital (r) has typically exceeded the rate of economic growth (g), and that as the gap between r and g widens, the concentration of wealth speeds up.

On the figures summarized from Piketty's book, the average return on capital held at roughly 4% to 5% for most of human history, rising above 5% during the Industrial Revolution and falling below 5% in the mid-20th century; global growth stayed just above 0% until the Industrial Revolution, then climbed toward 2%.
